report:
R1
- Behavior: Replace the hard-coded `EXPECTED_POST_CUTOFF` basename comparison with one oracle that classifies candidates from the sealed cutoff: frozen construction identity membership plus the sealed discovery predicates/filesystem boundaries and exact candidate identity. Partition the live walk all-and-only through that oracle; basename alone never establishes post-cutoff status.
- Deepest Owner: `test/legacy-case-a-migration-verifier.test.ts`, specifically its fixed-target construction-walk test and local sealed-predicate/candidate-identity functions.
- Red: Pass the same oracle a synthetic omitted frozen/pre-cutoff identity whose basename is `coder.ts` and require rejection. This counterexample exercises the real assertion path and would defeat the former basename allowlist.
- Green: The real source root produces 597 matched, 0 missing, 0 changed and the exact cutoff-derived partition; every accepted addition has identity evidence proving absence from the sealed pre-cutoff identity set, while the omitted pre-cutoff `coder.ts` is rejected.
- Scope: Change only the existing verifier for this regression. Add no parallel verifier/helper, do not recut the denominator, inspect payloads, or alter frozen migration evidence.

R2
- Behavior: Implement one closed, canonical association grammar in the existing verifier. Its source universe is exactly: (a) the frozen `inventory.json`/construction metadata for each of the 597 item keys, limited to `itemKey`, `basename`, and provenance/genericity/admission fields needed to select bytes; and (b) every byte source admitted for an item classified non-generic—repository bytes resolved from that item’s sealed reference tuple, and recovered/genuinely external source bytes bound by the item key and sealed source SHA-256. Recursively parse JSON objects/arrays and scan Markdown/plain text, but recursively omit every property named `issuePrCommitAssociations` (and its descendants) from derivation; the persisted disposition/recovered-index association fields under validation are comparison outputs only, never inputs. Reject generic JSONL/session/tool-event items before opening any payload.

  Freeze accepted forms as follows. Basenames accept only delimiter-bounded `issue-N`/`issue_N` and `pr-N`/`pr_N` tokens. Recursive JSON accepts a positive decimal issue number only under exact keys `issue`, `issueNumber`, or `issue_number`; a positive decimal PR number only under `pr`, `prNumber`, `pr_number`, `pullRequest`, `pullRequestNumber`, or `pull_request`; and a commit token only under `commit`, `commitOid`, `commitSha`, `headSha`, `reviewedHead`, or `targetHead`. Markdown/text accepts delimiter-bounded labels `issue #N`, `issue N`, `PR #N`, `PR N`, `pull request #N`, and `pull request N`, plus canonical repository-qualified `/issues/N` and `/pull/N` URLs whose host/owner/repository equal the sealed repository identity; commit text accepts only a token immediately labeled `commit`, `commitOid`, `commitSha`, `headSha`, `reviewedHead`, or `targetHead`. Matching is ASCII case-insensitive for labels/keys, decimal numbers are canonicalized to positive integers, and commit hex is lower-cased. Full commits require exactly 40 hex digits. Abbreviations require 7–39 hex digits and must resolve uniquely in the explicit commit universe reachable from the four sealed roots `ea64733e…`, `702e36f…`, `49807d4…`, and `da25044…` in the sealed local repository. Repository identity, each root, and the Git bytes used for repository-qualified links/reference resolution are ledgered as repository/full commit/path/blob/SHA-256 inputs; no ambient remote/ref or another repository may participate. Canonical output is sorted, deduplicated `{issues,pullRequests,commits}`, with null only when all three sets are empty.

  Freeze rejected boundaries through the same extractor: bare/unlabeled numbers or `#N`; issue-like numbers outside the listed basename delimiters/JSON keys/text labels; repository URLs for another host/owner/repository; arbitrary prose merely mentioning field names; hex under an unlisted JSON key, unlabeled hex, non-hex, fewer than 7 or more than 40 hex characters, ambiguous/unresolvable abbreviations, and a hex token embedded in a larger word. Structural values such as `commitOid`/`reviewedHead` are accepted only when they are actual listed JSON keys; prose discussing those names without the required immediate `label[:= ]token` form is rejected.
- Deepest Owner: The closed extractor, source selector, canonicalizer, resolver, and exact-set comparator in `test/legacy-case-a-migration-verifier.test.ts`; persisted outputs remain owned only by `.ak/dockets/issues/15/migration/legacy-case-a/dispositions.json` and `recovered-index.json`.
- Red: Table-drive every accepted and rejected boundary above through the same extractor/resolver used for real items. Then clone the actual parsed disposition/recovered record for second item `33454566…`, mutate its real `issuePrCommitAssociations` value (for example remove its resolved commit while preserving the derived inputs), and run that mutated record through the identical canonical exact-set comparator; require mismatch. Also mutate an eligible parsed source input for that item to a rejected boundary and require the derived set/comparison to change. Do not delete an expected-map entry. Retain the first known item check so both persisted metadata paths are exercised.
- Green: The bounded source universe deterministically derives one exact set per item; all eligible metadata, nested JSON, Markdown/text, recovered/external bytes, and referenced Git bytes are processed under the closed grammar, both persisted files equal the canonical sets exactly, accepted boundaries are recognized, rejected boundaries remain absent, and both real second-item mutations fail. Update only association fields whose values differ. No generic/excluded payload is opened.
- Scope: Change the existing verifier and only the association fields in the two current migration metadata files. Do not alter source/derivative/report bytes, broaden the grammar at Apply time, use ambient refs/remotes, inspect generic payloads, or change unrelated migration facts.

R3
- Behavior: Append a repair-003 Recorder closure with one independently executable child, result, and manifest/identity ledger. The child independently reruns corrected R1 and actual `scanBytes`; selection, dispositions, derivatives, and reports load from immutable Git inputs. Before import/execution it resolves and verifies the exact scanner-module bytes. The ledger records repository identity/full commit/path/blob OID/SHA-256 for every Git-resolvable discovery spec, walk, inventory, disposition, report, scanner, derivative, association-resolution input, and other repository input; every genuinely external source records item key, source SHA-256, and applicable frozen identity metadata only.
- Deepest Owner: New `.ak/dockets/issues/15/repair/repair-003/recorder-closure/` evidence: the child owns execution gates and the manifest owns immutable attribution.
- Red: Through the child’s assertion path, perturb representative tuple components, scanner hash, selection identity, source seal, complete hit report, cutoff identity, and each known-redacted record and require failure/nonzero. The sole verifier mechanically exercises these gates against stored successor evidence.
- Green: The child exits 0 only for 597 matched/0 missing/0 changed, a cutoff-derived all-and-only partition, exactly 277 selected sources, verified scanner bytes, matching source/derivative hashes and complete hit reports, and both redactions. Every tuple/seal resolves and hashes, the association resolution inputs are sealed, and no raw external-source duplicate is retained.
- Scope: Append only the new successor. Preserve repair-002 manifest, implementation, and result byte-for-byte, including seals `fd219ea9e1d43aae383d67a0289a92612726980e62b6a1aaf97fdacb19411576` and `654fdff4002b26cdaf08586b722aff6688b8c19b08752a62d329a84ef40e9a70`; preserve all earlier evidence. Do not share implementation with the seam verifier or retain scratch probes.

R4
- Behavior: Extend the sole verifier to resolve every successor Git tuple, verify every external seal/frozen-metadata binding and sealed association-resolution input, verify corrected exact association sets and real red mutations, and enforce preservation of all historical evidence at the forward target.
- Deepest Owner: Acceptance assertions in `test/legacy-case-a-migration-verifier.test.ts`, backed by the repository `typecheck` script and the new Recorder child/result gates.
- Red: Any tuple/seal mutation, association input/output mutation, historical blob/hash mutation, repair-002 seal mutation, source-count drift, source identity loss/change, scanner drift, incomplete hit report, missing redaction, or non-forward target fails the focused verifier or child. If any required 597 historical identity or 277 external identity is missing/changed, stop with evidence-bearing refusal rather than substitute a cutoff or denominator.
- Green: At a new strict forward descendant, `npm run typecheck` and `node --import tsx --test test/legacy-case-a-migration-verifier.test.ts` pass; the successor records child exit 0; every ledger and grammar boundary check passes; all four immutable commits remain ancestors; the four Receipt/manifest blob+SHA identities in `historical-nonconformance.json` re-resolve unchanged; and both repair-002 seals remain exact.
- Scope: Verification and preservation only. Do not change prior migration source bytes or any prior repair/Receipt/manifest/exhibit/result/historical-nonconformance bytes; no history rewrite, Case B, issues 16/17, session retention, generic/excluded-payload inspection, raw-source duplication, parallel verifier, or Soul/runtime/schema work. Planning performed read-only on a clean worktree; no edit or commit was made.
